name: Downtown Halifax
headline: Harbour air, with the city close at hand.
description: Downtown Halifax brings together the central business district, older commercial streets and the harbourfront. Waterfront walks, food stops and cultural outings make it a natural starting point for exploring the peninsula.
highlights: Walk the harbourfront boardwalk
Explore the older streets behind the waterfront
Build a food-and-culture loop through the centre
nuance: The peninsula is hilly and some streets are lively at night. Consider the actual walking route and immediate surroundings of your address.

name: North End
area: North of downtown on the Halifax peninsula
headline: Independent places, with a strong local story.
description: Halifax’s North End offers local businesses, café stops and streets with a distinctive community history. Exploring a small pocket on foot can reveal a different side of the peninsula from the main waterfront sights.
highlights: Explore local businesses around Agricola Street
Build a café-and-neighbourhood walking loop
Learn about the area’s African Nova Scotian history
nuance: North End covers a substantial area, and local pockets differ. Check where your address falls rather than assuming everything is close to downtown.

name: South End
headline: A quieter chapter beside the student city.
description: The South End combines university communities, older residential streets and access toward the peninsula’s southern green spaces. It can suit a daily rhythm built around walking, cafés and neighbourhood life.
highlights: Explore the residential streets around the universities
Plan an outing toward Point Pleasant Park
Find a local café away from the main visitor route
nuance: Student-oriented blocks and quieter residential streets offer different noise levels. Check the exact address and distances to the places you plan to visit.
